agency.name: Montana Department of Labor & Industry, Employment Relations Division (ERD), Workers' Compensation

ttd.basisLabel: Gross average weekly wage before taxes
ttd.rateText: 66 2/3% of the wages received at the time of injury, not more than the state's average weekly wage at the time of injury (MCA 39-71-701(3)).
ttd.minText: No minimum weekly TTD rate; the only statutory minimum ($596.00 for FY2027) applies to death benefits and never exceeds the decedent's actual wages.
ttd.periodLabel: injuries July 1, 2026 through June 30, 2027 (fiscal year 2027; FY2026 injuries July 1, 2025 - June 30, 2026: $1,137.00)

waiting.text: No compensation for the first 32 hours or 4 days of wage loss, whichever is less; benefits start on the 5th day. If the worker is totally disabled and unable to work for 21 days or longer, compensation is paid retroactively to the first day of total wage loss (MCA 39-71-736(1)).

ttdDuration.text: TTD is paid for the duration of the temporary disability, until maximum healing or release to the time-of-injury job or one with similar physical requirements; no fixed week cap (MCA 39-71-701(1), (3)).

ppd.text: PPD requires an actual wage loss and an AMA Guides 6th edition impairment rating (or Class 2+ impairment without wage loss for an impairment-only award). The whole-person rating plus statutory add-ons for age (1% if over 40), education (1% if under 12 years), wage loss (10% or 20%) and reduced labor capacity (up to 5%) is multiplied by 400 weeks (MCA 39-71-703); the weekly PPD rate is capped at $596.00 for FY2027 injuries.

facts.text: For FY2027 the state's average weekly wage was established at $1,192.06 and the Department adopted $1,192.00 as the maximum weekly rate for TTD, PTD, TPD, rehabilitation and death benefits (DLI memo, June 2026).
The PPD maximum is half the TTD maximum: $596.00 per week for injuries July 1, 2026 - June 30, 2027, over a 400-week schedule (ERD compensation rates chart).
Each day a worker elects sick leave counts toward the 4-day waiting period (MCA 39-71-736(2)).

TTD is not adjusted for cost of living, but permanent total disability benefits are, and PTD is paid until the worker is eligible for Social Security retirement benefits (MCA 39-71-701(3); 2026 Benefits Summary).
Montana State Fund operates the fraud hotline for claims it insures; other claims are reported to DLI (2026 Benefits Summary).
